failure.summary: Authentication integration tests failed due to missing environment variable

diagnosis.root_cause: Missing AUTH_SECRET_KEY environment variable in workflow configuration
diagnosis.technical_explanation: The OAuth authentication provider requires AUTH_SECRET_KEY to be set as an environment variable. The workflow configuration does not include this secret in the integration-tests job, causing the authentication initialization to fail when tests attempt to create OAuth sessions.
observed_facts: Stack trace shows failure in oauth_provider.py line 80
Workflow YAML does not define AUTH_SECRET_KEY in job environment
Other jobs in the workflow have the secret configured
Previous successful runs included this environment variable
inferences: The environment variable was likely removed or renamed during recent workflow refactoring
The failure is specific to the integration-tests job configuration
Unit tests pass because they mock the OAuth provider and don't require actual secrets
diagnosis.primary_vs_cascading: This is a primary failure. The missing environment variable is the root cause. All subsequent authentication-related test failures are cascading effects of this configuration issue.

alternative_hypotheses.description: Secret value was rotated and workflow secret was not updated
alternative_hypotheses.likelihood: Less likely. The error is KeyError indicating the variable is undefined, not an authentication failure which would suggest an invalid secret value.

alternative_hypotheses.description: Recent code change introduced a new secret dependency without updating CI
alternative_hypotheses.likelihood: Possible. The code expects AUTH_SECRET_KEY but this could be a new requirement. However, git history (if available) would clarify this.
